problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y+7z=-4 \\  & -x+3y-4z=5 \\  & x-2y+3z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a 3x3 System That Is Not in Row Echelon Form
examples.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079061/assets/3e66da254c5da8b28c86908dbe0d0100489db7ed9f1c752b2e253160b603ac45.png)
Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
examples.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079061/assets/1851c6530047d54eb28a337292ad4466caecade797c2cba39808eb85daf6e3e8.png)

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 4 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 2 \\ 5 & 4 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14079061/assets/f21067ccbed84ad8a3d52edb479d613f9291a0a51f34a4237ff7a42d25a1eb93.png)

So, we have the solution $x=3,$ $y=-2,$ and $z=0.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle 3,-2,0 \rangle.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y-3z=0 \\  & y+2z=0 \\  & z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form.

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x=2 \\  & y=4 \\  & z=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have he solution $x=2$, $y=4$ and $z=-2.$ Or, in vector form $⟨2,4,-2⟩.$
